topic: AWS Certified SysOps Administrator - Associate (SOA-C02) certification exam preparation - deploying, managing, and operating workloads on AWS, including monitoring and logging, reliability and business continuity, deployment and automation, security and compliance, networking and content delivery, and cost and performance optimization
exam_format: 65 questions, 130 minutes, delivered at Pearson VUE test centers or online-proctored. Multiple choice (one correct answer of four) and multiple response (two or more correct). Scaled score 100-1000 with a passing score of 720; compensatory scoring, so you do not need to pass each domain individually. NOTE: the exam previously included hands-on exam labs, but AWS REMOVED the exam labs (currently the exam is questions-only; AWS has described the removal as temporary, so verify the current format before your exam date). AWS recommends about one year of hands-on experience with AWS operations. The certification is valid for three years. Exam fee is USD 150 (plus tax where applicable) and varies by country; present any fee as approximate and advise candidates to confirm current AWS pricing.
question_types: multiple choice (single answer, exactly 4 options) and multiple response clearly marked as 'Select TWO/THREE'; every item is a real-world operations scenario asking which AWS service, configuration, or remediation is correct - NOT term definitions
audience: Systems administrators, cloud/DevOps engineers, site reliability engineers, and operations staff who deploy, manage, and operate workloads on AWS. AWS recommends 1+ year of hands-on experience with AWS operations, including monitoring, networking, security, and automation, plus comfort with the AWS Management Console and AWS CLI. A strong operations-focused companion to the AWS Solutions Architect Associate (SAA-C04), Developer Associate (DVA-C02), Data Engineer (DEA-C01), and Security Specialty (SCS-C03) courses already in this catalog.
author: Aseem Mankotia

domains.name: Monitoring, Logging, and Remediation
domains.notes: The heaviest domain. Implementing metrics, alarms, and filters with Amazon CloudWatch (metrics, custom metrics, CloudWatch Logs and Logs Insights, alarms, dashboards, CloudWatch agent), collecting and analyzing logs, and remediating issues based on monitoring output. Event-driven automation and remediation with Amazon EventBridge, AWS Systems Manager (Automation runbooks, Run Command, State Manager), and AWS Config rules. Choosing the correct monitoring, logging, or automated-remediation approach for a described operational scenario.

domains.name: Reliability and Business Continuity
domains.notes: Implementing scalability and elasticity (Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling, launch templates, scaling policies, Elastic Load Balancing target groups and health checks), high availability across Availability Zones and Regions, and backup/restore and disaster recovery (Amazon RDS snapshots and Multi-AZ, EBS snapshots, AWS Backup, S3 versioning and replication, Route 53 health checks and failover routing). Meeting a described RPO/RTO and SLA. Choosing the correct reliability or continuity design for a stated availability requirement.

domains.name: Deployment, Provisioning, and Automation
domains.notes: Provisioning and maintaining cloud resources: creating and managing AMIs, automating with AWS CloudFormation (templates, parameters, stacks, StackSets, drift detection, change sets) and AWS Systems Manager, managing multiple accounts, and deploying with services such as Elastic Beanstalk. Configuration management, patching (Systems Manager Patch Manager), and repeatable provisioning. Choosing the correct provisioning or automation mechanism for a described operations task.

domains.name: Security and Compliance
domains.notes: Implementing and managing security and compliance: AWS IAM (users, groups, roles, policies, least privilege, IAM Identity Center), data protection and encryption (AWS KMS, encryption at rest and in transit, ACM certificates, Secrets Manager, S3 access controls), and compliance/governance tooling (AWS Config, AWS CloudTrail, AWS Security Hub, Amazon GuardDuty, AWS Trusted Advisor). Choosing the correct security control, encryption approach, or compliance service for a described requirement.

domains.name: Networking and Content Delivery
domains.notes: Configuring and operating networking: Amazon VPC design (subnets, route tables, internet and NAT gateways, security groups vs network ACLs, VPC peering, VPC endpoints, Transit Gateway), hybrid connectivity (Site-to-Site VPN, Direct Connect), DNS with Amazon Route 53 (record types, routing policies, health checks), and content delivery/edge (Amazon CloudFront, global accelerator). Troubleshooting connectivity. Choosing the correct networking or content-delivery configuration for a described scenario.

domains.name: Cost and Performance Optimization
domains.notes: Managing cost and optimizing performance: cost visibility and controls (AWS Cost Explorer, AWS Budgets, Cost and Usage Report, cost allocation tags), purchasing options (On-Demand, Reserved Instances, Savings Plans, Spot), right-sizing (Compute Optimizer, Trusted Advisor), and performance optimization for compute, storage (EBS volume types, S3 storage classes), and databases. Choosing the correct cost-optimization or performance-tuning action for a described situation.

extra_guidance: AWS Certified SysOps Administrator - Associate (SOA-C02) is AWS's core OPERATIONS credential and completes the AWS associate set alongside the Solutions Architect and Developer associates. The exam is scenario-based - the real skill it tests is 'given this operational situation, which AWS service, configuration, or remediation is correct,' NOT memorizing definitions. IMPORTANT format note: SOA-C02 previously included hands-on EXAM LABS, but AWS REMOVED the exam labs - the exam is currently questions-only. State this clearly and tell candidates to verify the current format on AWS's official exam page before scheduling, since AWS has called the removal temporary. This is a READ-AND-UNDERSTAND operations course - show and explain real AWS CLI commands, CloudFormation/Systems Manager YAML/JSON, IAM policies, and CloudWatch alarm configs rather than requiring a live AWS account; make that explicit. Use EXACT current AWS service names: Amazon CloudWatch (Logs Insights, alarms, agent), Amazon EventBridge, AWS Systems Manager (Automation, Run Command, State Manager, Patch Manager), AWS Config, EC2 Auto Scaling, Elastic Load Balancing, Amazon RDS (Multi-AZ, snapshots), AWS Backup, Amazon S3 (versioning, replication, storage classes), AWS CloudFormation (StackSets, drift, change sets), AWS IAM and IAM Identity Center, AWS KMS, AWS Secrets Manager, AWS CloudTrail, AWS Security Hub, Amazon GuardDuty, AWS Trusted Advisor, Amazon VPC (security groups, NACLs, endpoints, Transit Gateway), AWS Direct Connect, Amazon Route 53, Amazon CloudFront, AWS Cost Explorer, AWS Budgets, Savings Plans, and AWS Compute Optimizer - with a one-line note that AWS evolves fast, so verify against current docs. The six domain names and weights above are AWS's official SOA-C02 exam-guide weights - use them verbatim. Note the 3-year validity and recommended 1 year of hands-on operations experience. Cover the classic SOA-C02 traps: security groups vs network ACLs, CloudWatch alarms vs EventBridge rules, Systems Manager Automation vs Lambda remediation, RDS Multi-AZ vs read replicas, Reserved Instances vs Savings Plans vs Spot, S3 storage classes and lifecycle, Route 53 routing policies, and EBS volume type selection. NEVER promise a pass or use the word 'guarantee' in ANY form (Udemy compliance) - use 'exam-focused preparation' framing throughout, including learning objectives and who-this-is-for. Present the exam fee as approximate (~USD 150, varies by country) and advise verifying current AWS pricing and the latest exam guide. The final chapter must be a full exam simulation with a 130-minute, 65-question time-management strategy. Scan the practice bank for stray other-vendor terms (Azure/Google/NVIDIA) before upload per the pipeline compliance rules.
